method: Reconcile the user-supplied diplomatic-academy and international-affairs control list against REV6. Promote only currently resolvable institutional entities; normalize successor names without duplicate IDs; retain unresolved/historical cases in watchlist.

normalizations.name: Sushma Swaraj Institute of Foreign Service (SSIFS)
normalizations.verification_status: VERIFIED — Ministry of External Affairs, Government of India primary source
normalizations.notes: Current canonical name. Established in 1986; formerly Foreign Service Training Institute / Foreign Service Institute. FSI was renamed Sushma Swaraj Institute of Foreign Service on 14 February 2020. This is an in-place normalization of A015, not a new institution.

additions.name: Hellenic Diplomatic Academy (HDA)
additions.verification_status: VERIFIED — Hellenic Ministry of Foreign Affairs primary source
additions.notes: Self-contained organic unit of the Hellenic Ministry of Foreign Affairs responsible for initial and continuing diplomatic training.

additions.name: Académie diplomatique et consulaire (ADC)
additions.verification_status: VERIFIED — France Diplomatie / MEAE primary source
additions.notes: Created in May 2024 as the dedicated initial and continuing training academy of the French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs. Historical references to the Institut diplomatique et consulaire are treated as predecessor/legacy context, not a separate current institution.

additions.name: Academia Diplomática de Chile Andrés Bello
additions.verification_status: VERIFIED — official academy primary source
additions.notes: Chile's diplomatic academy, created by decree on 3 June 1954; provides diplomatic formation and international cooperation.

additions.name: Academia Diplomática del Perú Javier Pérez de Cuéllar
additions.verification_status: VERIFIED — Peruvian Ministry of Foreign Affairs / state legal sources
additions.notes: Official Peruvian diplomatic academy; 2026 admissions, appointments and academic operations are documented by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

additions.name: Academia Diplomática del Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores y Movilidad Humana ‘Galo Plaza Lasso’
additions.verification_status: VERIFIED — Ecuador Ministry of Foreign Affairs primary source
additions.notes: Created in 1987, closed in 2011 and re-opened by presidential decision in 2018 / reintegrated into the Ministry in 2019; formally named for Galo Plaza Lasso in 2022 and active in the 2026–2027 training cycle.

additions.name: Diplomatic Academy, Australian Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT)
additions.institution_type: Government diplomatic learning and development academy
additions.verification_status: VERIFIED — Australian DFAT primary source
additions.notes: DFAT specialist learning and development hub for diplomatic tradecraft, foreign policy, trade, development and international engagement capability across the Australian Public Service.

additions.name: ADA University
additions.institution_type: State university and legal successor of Azerbaijan Diplomatic Academy
additions.verification_status: VERIFIED — ADA University primary source
additions.notes: Current legal entity. ADA University was established in 2014 and is the legal heir of Azerbaijan Diplomatic Academy, founded in 2006, and Information Technologies University. Azerbaijan Diplomatic Academy is therefore not counted separately.

additions.name: Foreign Service Academy (Pakistan)
additions.verification_status: VERIFIED — Pakistan Ministry of Foreign Affairs primary source
additions.notes: Training arm of Pakistan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs; provides entry-level, mid-career and international diplomatic courses.

additions.name: Foreign Service Academy (Bangladesh)
additions.verification_status: VERIFIED — Bangladesh Ministry of Foreign Affairs / FSA primary sources
additions.notes: Sole specialist diplomatic training institute of Bangladesh. Current official MFA institutional history places establishment of the present FSA in 1996; earlier foreign-affairs training structures are predecessor context.

additions.name: Foreign Service Institute (Philippines)
additions.institution_type: Government diplomatic training and foreign-policy research institute
additions.verification_status: VERIFIED — Foreign Service Institute primary source
additions.notes: Established by Presidential Decree 1060 on 9 December 1976; serves as the Philippine foreign service's training, professional-development and research institution.

additions.name: Bandaranaike International Diplomatic Training Institute (BIDTI)
additions.verification_status: VERIFIED — BIDTI primary source
additions.notes: Established in September 1995 for advanced training in diplomacy and international relations; since 2006 vested under the Lakshman Kadirgamar Institute framework by parliamentary act.

additions.name: Institut des Relations Internationales du Cameroun (IRIC)
additions.institution_type: University institute for diplomacy and international relations
additions.verification_status: VERIFIED — IRIC and University of Yaoundé II primary sources
additions.notes: Institute of the University of Yaoundé II with dual higher-education / external-relations institutional context; includes Diplomacy and Professional Training and a diplomatic internship/continuing-training cycle.

additions.name: Institute for Diplomatic Studies, Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Egypt
additions.verification_status: VERIFIED — Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs primary source
additions.notes: Specialized governmental institution and principal MFA training arm for Egyptian diplomatic and consular personnel; operations began in June 1966.

additions.name: Academia Diplomática Venâncio de Moura (ADVM)
additions.verification_status: VERIFIED — ADVM and Angola MIREX primary sources
additions.notes: Angolan Ministry of External Relations diplomatic academy created by Presidential Decree 5/21 of 4 January 2021; inaugurated in November 2020. Successor context includes the former Institute / Higher Institute of International Relations, whose higher-education function was reorganized in 2020.

additions.name: Mohamed bin Mubarak Al Khalifa Academy for Diplomatic Studies (MBMA)
additions.verification_status: VERIFIED — MBMA primary source
additions.notes: Established by Royal Decree on 1 August 2019 and succeeded the Diplomatic Institute of Bahrain's Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The predecessor Diplomatic Institute is not counted separately.

additions.name: Institute of Diplomacy and Foreign Relations (IDFR)
additions.verification_status: VERIFIED — IDFR / Ministry of Foreign Affairs Malaysia primary source
additions.notes: Established on 1 July 1991 and operating as Malaysia's Ministry of Foreign Affairs training institute; provides diplomatic training, research, consultancy and international capacity building.

additions.name: The Diplomatic Institute (Israel)
additions.institution_type: Private diplomacy, diplomatic-support and training organization
additions.verification_status: VERIFIED — active institutional primary source; legal-form status not independently characterized by WPA
additions.notes: Private/non-government institutional bridge serving diplomats and embassies through diplomacy training, seminars, analysis and professional support. Explicitly not represented as an official institute of Israel's Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

additions.name: Egmont — Royal Institute for International Relations
additions.institution_type: Independent public-utility foreign-policy think tank and diplomatic training institute
additions.verification_status: VERIFIED — Egmont Institute primary source
additions.notes: Brussels-based independent think tank with research, policy dialogue and specialized training programmes for diplomats and foreign professionals.

additions.name: South African Institute of International Affairs (SAIIA)
additions.institution_type: Independent public-policy and international-affairs think tank
additions.verification_status: VERIFIED — SAIIA primary source
additions.notes: Founded in 1934; independent African foreign-policy and international-affairs think tank focused on research, dialogue and policy engagement.

additions.name: Elliott School of International Affairs, George Washington University
additions.verification_status: VERIFIED — George Washington University primary source
additions.notes: Specialist school educating international-affairs professionals and conducting policy-relevant global research in Washington, D.C.

additions.name: Johns Hopkins School of Advanced International Studies (SAIS)
additions.institution_type: University school of advanced international studies
additions.verification_status: VERIFIED — Johns Hopkins SAIS primary source
additions.notes: Founded in 1943; graduate school focused on international affairs, policy, economics, strategy and leadership, with Washington and international campuses/programmes.

additions.name: Columbia University — School of International and Public Affairs (SIPA)
additions.institution_type: University school of international and public affairs
additions.verification_status: VERIFIED — Columbia SIPA primary source
additions.notes: Founded in 1946 as the School of International Affairs; specialist professional school in international affairs and public policy.

additions.name: American University — School of International Service (SIS)
additions.verification_status: VERIFIED — American University primary source
additions.notes: Founded in 1957; specialist school offering international-affairs education and research across diplomacy-adjacent fields.

additions.name: King’s College London — Department of War Studies
additions.institution_type: University department for security, conflict and international relations
additions.verification_status: VERIFIED — King’s College London primary source
additions.notes: Department within the School of Security Studies focused on conflict, security, defence and international relations; included as strategic/security academic context, not core protocol training.

additions.name: University of Copenhagen — Department of Political Science / International Relations research group
additions.verification_status: VERIFIED — University of Copenhagen primary source
additions.notes: International Relations research group within the Department of Political Science; covers diplomacy, international organizations, governance, security, geopolitics and related fields.

additions.name: Helena Z. Benitez School of International Relations and Diplomacy, Philippine Women’s University
additions.institution_type: University school of international relations and diplomacy
additions.verification_status: VERIFIED — Philippine Women’s University primary source
additions.notes: Specialist university school offering foreign-service and diplomacy education with diplomatic and consular theory/practice, international law and global governance.

additions.name: Diplomacy Training Program (DTP)
additions.verification_status: VERIFIED — UNSW primary source
additions.notes: Independent Australian NGO affiliated with UNSW, founded in 1989, providing human-rights advocacy and people’s-diplomacy training across the Asia-Pacific. Not represented as an ANU/UNSW diplomatic academy.

entity_resolution.A015: Current canonical name SSIFS; former Indian Foreign Service Institute / FSI aliases do not create a new record.
entity_resolution.A041: Existing Anwar Gargash Diplomatic Academy record also resolves historical Emirates Diplomatic Academy naming; no duplicate added in REV7.
entity_resolution.A072: Current French Académie diplomatique et consulaire; legacy Institut diplomatique et consulaire reference is not separately counted.
entity_resolution.A077: ADA University is the legal heir of Azerbaijan Diplomatic Academy; predecessor is not separately counted.
entity_resolution.A085: MBMA succeeded Bahrain's Diplomatic Institute; predecessor is not separately counted.
entity_resolution.A050: Existing Türkiye MFA Diplomacy Academy already resolves the user-list Turkey entry; no duplicate added.

watchlist_append.name: Academia Diplomática ‘José de Marcoleta’ (Nicaragua)
watchlist_append.classification: legally established diplomatic academy / current operational status pending
watchlist_append.reason: Nicaraguan legal framework explicitly establishes the academy under the Foreign Ministry and defines its training mandate, but a sufficiently current academy-specific operational source was not resolved in this pass. Retain outside canonical counts until current activity is independently confirmed.

watchlist_append.name: Asia-Pacific College of Diplomacy, Australian National University
watchlist_append.reason: Strong historical relevance, but the current institutional successor/organizational form needs exact resolution before canonical insertion to avoid duplicating other ANU structures.

watchlist_append.name: University of International Relations — Center for International Education (Beijing)
watchlist_append.reason: The parent university is identifiable, but the exact current Center for International Education entity and diplomacy-specific status were not resolved to canonical threshold in this pass.

watchlist_append.name: Institut des hautes études internationales (Burkina Faso)
watchlist_append.reason: Historical foreign-ministry training references exist, but present institutional name, status and operational continuity were not sufficiently resolved.
